newsitem.title: UK: Copper steadier on LME pre-market, aluminium firms.
newsitem.headline: Copper steadier on LME pre-market, aluminium firms.

text.p: Copper prices clawed their way higher during Tuesday LME pre-market trading, injecting an undercurrent of steadier sentiment throughout the metals complex.
Traders said conditions were not over-active, however, and there were signs that further advances would be difficult to sustain in some metals given overhead resistance levels.
"Copper has led the way, and it is dragging the others up by their bootstraps," one said.

Factors behind the upswing in copper were the modest 1,875-tonne fall in stocks, the widening in the cash/threes backwardation to $71/75 from $60/65 on Monday, and the ongoing strike at Chile's Escondida mine.
The strike by some workers at the world's largest mine has lasted three days and operations at are at 85 percent of normal levels.
Three months copper prices touched a high of $2,303 and then settled at $2,300, up $11.50 from Monday. There is likely to be stern resistance above $2,300, traders added.
Aluminium was buttressed by a 4,700-tonne decline in LME stocks and a 24-hour strike at Alcoa Australia, although output has not been hit.
Prices pushed through $1,570, triggering some buy-stops, with recent trade at $1,576, up $22 a tonne from Monday.
Elsewhere the advances were more modest, with lead gaining $5 at $633 while zinc rose $7 to $1,255.
Tin pushed up to $5,750, a gain of $40, while nickel nudged back above $7,400 to trade at $7,420, also up $40.
Aluminium alloy was indicated at $1,455/65 a tonne, up from Monday's $1,447 close.
